# All Functions and Features

Every function the engine answers to, alphabetically, with the
maturity rung it has actually earned.

**Generated by `tools/gen_version_ladder.qu`. Do not edit.** The
names come from the interpreter's own dispatch table and the
evidence is re-scraped on every run, so this page cannot claim a
function the engine lacks, omit one it has, or keep asserting a
rung after the evidence for it goes away.

## Project version: `0.1.0-2.x`

Computed, not declared: it is the lowest rung any function sits
on. The version rises when the weakest function rises, which is
the only reading of a version number that cannot be optimistic.

## The ladder

| Rung | Stage | What it means | Who may grant it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.1.0-1.asp` | Aspire | An idea being looked at. Interesting? Useful? | anyone; a no goes to `Garbage.txt` |
| `0.1.0-2.x` | Next | Experimental. Exists; nothing proves it works. | computed |
| `0.1.0-3.a` | Alpha | At least one test executes it. | computed |
| `0.1.0-4.aplus` | Alpha++ | Executed AND its speed measured against MATLAB/Python/Matty. | computed |
| `0.2.0-5.b` | Beta | Tried repeatedly, with varied inputs, by a person. | **Ahmed only** |
| `0.3.0-6.rc` | RC | User-tested; on par with or better than Python/MATLAB. | **Ahmed only** |
| `0.4.0` | Public | No private leak, no debug data, released. | **Ahmed only** |

These are real version strings, not labels: `cargo` accepts every
one of them, which `v0.01a` and `v0.010a` could not -- a leading
zero in the minor field is rejected outright. Two consequences of
using semver honestly are visible above. Alpha++ is spelled
`aplus` because `+` introduces build metadata in semver and would
be discarded from the comparison. And each stage carries a NUMBER
before its name, because pre-release tags sort alphabetically --
left to themselves `-a` would sort below `-asp`, putting Alpha
beneath Aspire and inverting the ladder. A leading `1.`..`6.`
sorts numerically, so the order above is the order semver reads.

The line between the computed rungs and the signed ones is the
point of this file. Evidence can show that a function is
exercised and measured. It cannot show that someone tried it with
awkward inputs and was satisfied. So this tool stops at
`0.1.0-4.aplus`, and Beta upward needs a row in `versions/ladder.tsv`
carrying a signature, a date, and what was actually tried.

## Aspire (`0.1.0-1.asp`) -- ideas under consideration

Not in the engine. Listed here so that looking around has
somewhere to land other than memory. A no moves the row to
`Garbage.txt` with its reasoning intact.

| Idea | Where it came from | Verdict so far |
|---|---|---|
| Strict canonical lowering of method calls (`sig.fft()` beside `fft(sig)`) | Qu-Aspire lane; agent_co.txt review 2026-09-10 | needs-a-decision-from-Ahmed -- methods already exist; choose strict lowering versus compatibility exceptions for modules, GUI and callable record fields. Existing function-variable shadowing differs between forms (99 versus 2). See agent_co.txt for AST rule, evidence and demonstration gate; no maturity promotion. |
| Making OOP less prominent in the public demos | 2026-09-09 public-release hygiene audit; agent_co.txt review 2026-09-10 | pursue -- repair the existing first-session route, absent README example path and conflicting installation instructions; current beginner chapters and README already use flat scientific code. Defer advanced notation, do not create another tutorial. Human demonstration gate in agent_co.txt. |
| Executable call contracts and local help for five beginner builtins | Observed help("mean") output; agent_co.txt review 2026-09-10 | pursue -- bounded experiment for mean, fft, plot, size and read_csv using shared validation/help facts and runnable Qu examples; compare with reference links and drop if it requires a duplicate unchecked registry. No engine implementation or maturity promotion. |
| Slot-resolve every name at parse time, not only inside fast loops | Performance assessment relayed by Ahmed 2026-09-10; agent_co follow-up in agent_co.txt | PURSUE -- premise VERIFIED: env is HashMap<String, Value> (lib.rs:3301) and frames Vec<HashMap<String, Value>> (3314), so each name read outside the fast path hashes a string. Register machinery already exists to extend: FastExpr (3909), eval_fast(e, regs: &[f64]) (3921), CompiledFn (4769). Needs no JIT. |
| Widen the fast path to allow calls to pure numeric builtins inside fast loops | Same assessment | OPEN, but its headline example is STALE: the "while is 29x slower" figure was fixed -- BACKLOG.md:377 marks it [x], "measured at 1.1x now". The remaining claim (any call in the body ejects the loop to the tree walker) was NOT verified. Measure before scoping. |
| Fuse array expressions (Y = A .* B + C) into one element loop before evaluating | agent_co follow-up 2026-09-10, agent_co.txt | PURSUE per agent_co. Removes one intermediate array: 6 logical element reads/writes become 4. agent_co is explicit that this does NOT establish a speedup -- caches, compile cost, SIMD and size all matter. Gate: measure correctness, elapsed, prep, repeat-call time and allocated bytes on small AND large arrays; cover NaN/inf/signed-zero and aliasing; no FP reassociation or fma contraction that changes rounding. |
| Cache prepared execution plans and widen the existing scalar register tier | agent_co follow-up 2026-09-10, agent_co.txt | PURSUE per agent_co, CONDITIONAL on profiles showing repeated preparation is material. Note it corrects a common misreading: whole-function caching already EXISTS (CompiledFn ~4769), so this is extension, not a new subsystem. Gate: record cache hit/miss and prep cost, compare cold vs repeat, then redefine a function or change an input type and verify invalidation. |
| SIMD on fused kernels, plus output explaining why a computation was not optimized | agent_co follow-up 2026-09-10, agent_co.txt | PURSUE per agent_co, but ONLY after a fused baseline exists. Warns wider vectors do not fix memory traffic, and SIMD reductions may alter floating-point order. The explanation output must describe the actual chosen plan, not a separately maintained claim -- otherwise it becomes another lying surface. |
| Codex full audit 2026-09-11: 10 further ideas (N-D arrays, fit/optimizer state, filtfilt boundary policy, inverse STFT, stateful block filtering, sparse linear algebra, tensor/layer API, bounded array fusion, unified callable resolution, help provenance) | agent_co (Codex) audit, agent_co.txt; full report and runnable probes at .claude/worktrees/codex-qu-audit-20260911/docs/reviews/qu-audit-2026-09-11.{md,qu} plus captured output | OPEN. Three are marked needs-a-decision-from-Ahmed: unit contract, tensor/layer API, unified flat-vs-method callable resolution. The rest are pursue with stated gates. Codex ran against master snapshot 3cca8198 on an isolated branch after finding the ROOT checkout parked and 286 commits behind -- it did not use the parked tree as an oracle. |
| File-level `import` is a flat include, not a module | Qu-Aspire lane; Ahmed 2026-09-11: "is a file acting as a class, can we make it a module instead" | OPEN -- premise VERIFIED. `import "mymod.qu"` copies EVERYTHING from the file into the caller scope, functions and top-level variables alike, with no qualified form. Probe: mymod.qu holding SECRET=123 and function helper(a); main.qu doing import "mymod.qu" then print(helper(5)) => 10 and print(SECRET) => 123. The namespaced spelling does not exist: print(mymod.helper(5)) => "`mymod` is not defined". So a .qu file behaves as a flat include whose private state leaks, which is what makes it feel like a class rather than a module. Two open sub-questions for whoever takes this: (1) native modules DECLARE namespacing -- MODULE_EXPORTS lists ("xlsx", read/sheets/write) and ("codec", ...) -- so the mechanism exists in the engine, but I could not reach it: import "xlsx" looks for a FILE and fails, and bare xlsx.read says "`xlsx` is not defined". Either there is a third spelling I did not find or the namespaced native path is unreachable; establish which BEFORE designing on top of it. (2) Scoping inside functions is already correct and does not need changing: assignment is local (x=1 outside, x=99 inside, prints 1), reads fall through (prints 8), and `global` writes through (prints 42). |

## Every function

`tests` counts call sites in the test corpus -- the `tests/`
directories and the interpreter's own `#[cfg(test)]` region.
`bench` counts them under `benchmarks/`, `ex` under `catalog/`
and `example_codes/`. `doc` is whether a stdlib chapter
describes it. A call site is counted, not a bare word, because
`add`, `all`, `box` and `min` are ordinary English.

**A caution about the `doc` column: it is currently `yes` for
every one of the 838 builtins.** A column with one value
carries no information, and the readiness gate that reads it is
therefore weaker than its wording suggests -- Beta-ready reduces
to two tests, RC-ready to three tests plus a benchmark or an
example. It is still computed rather than removed, so that an
undocumented builtin landing tomorrow makes the column start
discriminating again and this paragraph stop being true. Until
then, read `doc` as a fact about the chapters, not about any
individual function.
